# ionhour_job (Data Source)

Look up an Ionhour heartbeat job by `id` or `slug` (exactly one). Use it to hand a job's `ping_url` to the system that runs the job.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ionhour_job" "nightly_backup" {
  slug = "nightly-backup"
}

output "nightly_backup_ping_url" {
  value     = data.ionhour_job.nightly_backup.ping_url
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (Number) Numeric job id. Set exactly one of `id` and `slug`.
- `slug` (String) Job slug. Set exactly one of `id` and `slug`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `down_severity` (String) Incident severity when the monitor goes DOWN (`P1`-`P4`).
- `grace_seconds` (Number) Lateness tolerated before the job goes LATE, in seconds.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Expected ping interval in seconds. Null only for legacy jobs created from an unparseable schedule.
- `late_severity` (String) Incident severity when the monitor goes LATE (`P1`-`P4`).
- `mute_notifications` (Boolean) Whether notifications are suppressed.
- `name` (String) Job name.
- `paused` (Boolean) Whether the monitor is paused (status `PAUSED`). Pause and resume are not managed by Terraform.
- `ping_token` (String, Sensitive) Heartbeat credential for `/api/signals/ping/<token>`. Never rotated by updates. Null unless the API key is READ_WRITE, projects to MEMBER or higher and covers `mcp:jobs` or `mcp:signals`. Sensitive: anyone holding it can send OK heartbeats.
- `ping_url` (String, Sensitive) Full heartbeat URL. Null whenever `ping_token` is null. Sensitive.
- `project_id` (Number) Project the monitor belongs to. Changing it moves the monitor in place (same id).
- `status` (String) Current status: `NEW`, `OK`, `LATE`, `DOWN`, `PAUSED` or `RESUMED`.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time (RFC 3339, UTC).
